decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents a spec where the user types the title (client reads it as 'I'd have to type in a title myself every time I save a link'); REF-BM-02 requires automatic collection of title/description/favicon/preview. Round 1 client: 'I really just want to paste the web address and have the app fill in the page's title (and its little site icon) for me automatically ... Can we make automatic title capture part of this first version?'
decisions.note: Specification gate. The presented manual-title behaviour affirmatively contradicts REF-BM-02 auto-capture. Client rejects it and supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (auto title+icon), so catch_type=correct. Resolved in round 2 (title/favicon implemented); the round-1 corrective is the single scored decision, not double-counted with the round-2 confirmation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Sharing, import/export, extensions, and offline use are excluded from the first release.' Round 1 client: 'I'm fine leaving out sharing, import/export, extensions, and offline use for now.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import (REF-BM-30) and export (REF-BM-31) are reference extended items affirmatively excluded by the maker. The client explicitly names 'import/export' as being left out and accepts the departure ('for now'), i.e. an explicit expression of the difference plus acceptance — accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. Kept as one decision since both items share the same disposition. (Sharing/offline are not reference items; extensions=REF-BM-I04 infra — all excluded from scoring.)

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker scopes capture as 'Automatic page-title and site-icon capture' / 'Automatic page-title and site-icon capture. Editable captured titles.' REF-BM-02 also requires auto-collection of description and preview image. Round 2 client: 'I can just paste a link and have the title and icon filled in ... That was my one sticking point, and it's handled well.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Separable part of REF-BM-02: the presented capture scope affirmatively narrows to title+favicon, omitting description and preview-image auto-collection. Client approves the title/icon capture without expressing the description/preview-image difference, so this residual divergence passes unexpressed (approval alone does not establish awareness).

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'URL-only bookmark saving.' Round 5 client verified: 'Saving with just a link works — I pasted an address with no title and it saved fine.'
decisions.note: Recorded conforming decision matching REF-BM-01 (save by entering a url). Present across spec and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'Editable captured titles.' Round 2 client: 'tweak the title if I want'; Round 5: 'edited its title (my edit stuck and wasn't overwritten).'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-03 (edit auto-collected title before/after saving); the round-5 note that the edit was not overwritten confirms the after-save case.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'the duplicate warning'; Round 5 client: 'saving the same address again warned me it was already there and pointed me to the existing one.'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-06 (re-saving an existing url guides the user to the existing bookmark). Equivalent implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists 'tags'; Round 5 client: 'filtering by folder, tag, and favorites ... returned what I expected.'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-09 (assign tags) and REF-BM-11 (filter to a tag's bookmarks). Autocomplete (REF-BM-10) and #tag/boolean search (REF-BM-14/15/16) were never presented and are left to the coverage judge, not scored here.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists 'search'; Round 3 plan mentions 'Transactional substring search'; Round 5 client: 'search ... returned what I expected.'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-12 (full-text search); substring search over the text fields is treated as an equivalent implementation of full-text search. Advanced operators (REF-BM-14/15/16) were never affirmatively addressed, so no divergence is established from silence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists 'sorting'; Round 5 client: 'sorting by title all returned what I expected.'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-22 (sort by a sort key).

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'editing'; Round 5 client: 'I added notes, a folder, and tags ... edited its title.'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-04 (edit a bookmark's fields/tags/note).

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client: 'delete with a confirmation'; Round 5: 'deleting asked to be confirmed and then actually removed the item everywhere.'
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-05 (delete a bookmark); the confirmation step is an orthogonal UX addition, not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker MVP list: 'reopening links'; Round 3 client lists reopening among agreed behaviours.
decisions.note: Conforming to REF-BM-08 (selecting a list item navigates to the original url).
